yeoman.definition: An official providing honorable service in a royal or high noble household, ranking between a squire and a page. Especially, a yeoman of the guard, a member of a ceremonial bodyguard to the UK monarch (not to be confused with a Yeoman Warder).

yeomanly.definition: Like a yeoman: stout and true.

yeomanry.definition: A class of small freeholders who cultivated their own land.

yeomen.definition: An official providing honorable service in a royal or high noble household, ranking between a squire and a page. Especially, a yeoman of the guard, a member of a ceremonial bodyguard to the UK monarch (not to be confused with a Yeoman Warder).

yerd.definition: A yard, plot of ground around a building or fenced paddock.

yern.definition: To have a strong desire for something or to do something; to long for or to do something.

yes.definition: An affirmative expression; an answer that shows agreement or acceptance.

yet.definition: Thus far; up to the present; up to some unspecified time.

yew.definition: A species of coniferous tree, Taxus baccata, with dark-green flat needle-like leaves and seeds bearing red arils, native to western, central and southern Europe, northwest Africa, northern Iran and southwest Asia.

yield.definition: To give as a result or outcome; to produce or render.

yielded.definition: To give as a result or outcome; to produce or render.

yielding.definition: To give as a result or outcome; to produce or render.

yoke.definition: The yellow, spherical part of an egg that is surrounded by the white albumen, and serves as nutriment for the growing young.

yonder.definition: At or in a distant but indicated place.

you.definition: To address (a person) using the pronoun you (in the past, especially to use you rather than thou, when you was considered more formal).

young.definition: In the early part of growth or life; born not long ago.

youngest.definition: In the early part of growth or life; born not long ago.

youth.definition: The quality or state of being young.
